High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Mahendra Choubey - Advocate for appellant.
Shri Yadvendra Dwivedi - Panel Lawyer for State.
Shri Sheshraj Kushwaha - Advocate for respondent No.2.
Heard on admission.
The appeal seems to be arguable, hence admitted for final hearing.

Also heard on I.A. No.18797 of 2025, a first application under Section 430 of BNSS, 2023 for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail to appellant-Ritik Rajak.
This criminal appeal assails the judgment dated 29.07.2025 passed in Special Case No.11 of 2024 by the learned Special Judge, Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, District Sagar (M.P.), whereby present appellant has been convicted under Sections 376(1) and 366 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo 10 years R.I. with fine of Rs.1,000/- and five years R.I. with fine of Rs.1,000/- respectively, with default stipulations.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The appellant has further been convicted under Section 363 of IPC and Section 3 r/w 4(1) of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, however, no separate sentence has been awarded by the learned trial Court for these offence.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the present appellant that the appellant and the prosecutrix have solemnized the marriage, and the 2 CRA-7614-2025 prosecutrix is now pregnant.
In light of this compromise between the parties, a lenient view should be adopted by the Court.

Though the period of custody is only one month, having regard to the fact that the prosecutrix initially did not level any allegations of rape and other offence against the present appellant, and the initial allegations were of abduction only.
It was only after the DNA report was received and the prosecutrix was examined then she leveled allegations of rape and other offences against the appellant.

It is also submitted that, in view of the contradictions and variations that appeared in the prosecutrix's statement mainly in paragraphs 13, 14, and 15, the veracity of her statement becomes doubtful.

Keeping in view the contradictions, variations and factum of compromise between the parties and the fact that initially the allegation of rape etc. has not been leveled against the present appellant, the present appellant deserves suspension of sentence.
It is further submitted that the DNA report is also negative.

The appellant is ready to abide by all the conditions as may be imposed Accused X vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46181350/
1 by this Court.

entities.text: Accused X vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no likelihood of early hearing of the instant appeal in near future.
In view of the aforesaid, learned counsel for the appellant prays for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
Per contra, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the victim/respondent No.2 has expressed his no objection on the application for suspension of sentence.
On the other hand, the learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the application on the ground that the period of custody is very short, with only one month custody is there.

Moreover,
since the prosecutrix 3 CRA-7614-2025 was a minor, the consent of prosecutrix as indicated by the learned counsel has no legal significance.
It is contended that subsequent compromise does not render any support to the appellant.
There is ample evidence against the present appellant and the learned trial Court has rightly convicted the present appellant.

Considering the rival contentions of the parties, evidence available on record, period of custody and having regard to the attending facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the opinion that it is not a fit case where benefit of suspension of sentence should be granted to the appellant at this stage.
Accordingly, I.A. No.18797 of 2025 is dismissed.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE THK Accused X vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46181350/
